[MUQATIL:44:44-50/r10] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Aziz means impregnable, while karim here means self-honoring or conceited.
[MUQATIL:44:44-50/r11] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | Abu Jahl used to boast in worldly life that he was the mightiest and noblest of Quraysh; the keeper taunts him with that claim in Hell.

[FARISI-HUJJA:v6p166#2/r4] FARISI-HUJJA, d. 377 · author | holds | The source also cites Abu Jahl's boast that he was the mightiest and most protective man in the valley.

[THALABI:v8p355#2/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The taunt is directed at Abu Jahl, who claimed nobody between the two ends of Mecca was more powerful or noble than he.

[MAWARDI-FULL:v5p257/r13] MAWARDI-FULL, d. 450 · قتادة | reports | Qatada says this taunt was revealed concerning Abu Jahl.

[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v7p350#3/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Calling him mighty and noble is a taunt; Abu Jahl used to claim he was Quraysh's most powerful and honored man.
